item.title: Cost of Living in Essendon 2026: Rent, Food & the Real Numbers
item.description:

Rent: The Big Number

item.title: Essendon for Young Professionals 2026: Lifestyle, Cost & Nightlife
item.description:
Young professionals in Essendon tend to love some things and tolerate others. The suburb sits 10km northwest of the CBD on the Craigieburn line, and its strengths — reliable transport, good food, and quiet residential streets — come with trade-offs around nightlife and social scene. Here is the honest breakdown.

The Young Professional Scorecard

What Matters Grade Reality Check
Nightlife & Bars C+ Wine bars on Rose St, pubs for footy, CBD for big nights
Food Scene B+ Italian dining is strong, Rose St and Keilor Rd deliver
Commute to CBD B+ 18-22 min by train to Flagstaff
Rent Affordability B 1BR ~$350/pw, decent for the northwest
Walkability B Rose St walkable, car helps for broader area
Social Scene B+ Sporting clubs and community events, less bar-focused

The After-Work Scene

Essendon has enough for a weeknight drink — a few wine bars and pubs on Rose Street that attract a post-work crowd. The Italian restaurants along Rose Street and Keilor Road double as social spots for dinner and drinks. For anything more substantial, the CBD is about 20 minutes by train, and Moonee Ponds (one stop south) has additional options along Puckle Street.

item.title: Transport in Essendon 2026: Trains, Trams & the Commute Reality
item.description:
Essendon’s transport game scored B+ in our latest review. Here is what that actually means for your daily commute. Sitting 10km northwest of the CBD, Essendon has reliable train access and reasonable road connections, though it lacks direct tram service.

Transport Scorecard

Mode Available Quality Notes
Train ✅ Good Craigieburn line, regular peak service
Tram ❌ None No direct tram — train and bus only
Bus ✅ Average Cross-suburban connections, variable frequency
Cycling ✅ Adequate Creek trail plus flat residential streets
Driving ✅ Good CityLink access, street parking available

Getting to the CBD

By train: Essendon station is on the Craigieburn line. Trains to Flagstaff take about 18 to 22 minutes during peak, running every 8 to 12 minutes. Off-peak services run every 15 to 20 minutes. This is the most reliable commute option.
